meta.triageRationale: One cohesive Story under one design: a reach computation from the session worker's handler runtime, a classified inventory fixture with a guard test, and moving any value that needs one copy to its owner. It has real design choices (how to compute reach over imports, the classification scheme, how the guard detects new state) and several tasks, but it is not a new subsystem and decomposes into no independent stories. The closest existing machinery is the session-source inventory test and fixture (partial match: it scans boundary sites, not module-scope state), so it extends a known pattern rather than inventing one. The inventory is large (the session worker imports 19 modules directly and the text search for module-scope mutable declarations under src/daemon hit its cap), which rules out small.

summary.prose: This Story writes down, for every module-scope variable or container that a daemon session worker can load and that holds changing state, whether a separate copy per thread is correct, whether the value lives in a cross-thread store, or whether exactly one thread must own it, and why. A test-side compiler scanner finds those declarations from the session worker's imports, and a guard test fails when one appears or disappears without a matching entry in a reviewed inventory file. Any value that needs a single copy but does not have one yet is given its owner the way Story s3 did for the chat pool, the todos bus, the understanding service and the run registry.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Classify module-scope mutable state reachable from session handlers and guard it

api.name: moduleStateInventory
api.signature: moduleStateInventory(root: string): ModuleStateSite[]  // new, test-side, beside connectionSourceInventory; interface ModuleStateSite { readonly key: string /* '<file>#<name>' */; readonly file: string; readonly name: string; readonly kind: 'let' | 'var' | 'container' | 'literal' }

returns.meaning: Every top-level declaration, in the static and dynamic import closure of src/daemon/threads/session-worker.ts (value imports within src/, excluding __tests__ and *.test.ts), that holds mutable state: each `let`/`var`; each `const` bound to a constructed instance (new X) other than a frozen one; and each `const` array/object literal that is not `as const`/Object.freeze'd and that the type checker finds written somewhere in the program (assignment, property write, or a mutating call such as set/add/delete/clear/push/pop/shift/unshift/splice/sort). Sorted by key.

dataModelChanges.details: A reviewed JSON file beside the new test, keyed by '<file>#<name>' for every site moduleStateInventory returns. Each entry: class 'per-thread' (a separate copy per thread is correct: a cache of immutable or re-readable data, a test seam, a per-thread handle over a shared file or block, logger or diagnostic setup, or a value only used on a thread class that is not a session worker), 'shared-store' (the state is kept in a cross-thread store: the shared lock block, the status board, LMDB/Lance files) or 'one-owner' (exactly one thread may hold it); for one-owner an owner naming the thread and how calls reach it (shared-state worker via SHARED_STATE_METHODS/inDaemonTarget, main thread, admin worker or indexing worker); and a reason of at least 40 characters. No source or site digests: editing a classified file never fails the guard.

Before: only the four s3 families (chat pool src/daemon/chat-handler.ts, todos bus src/daemon/todos-rpc.ts, understanding service: the module-scope client `understanding` in src/daemon/threads/session-worker.ts:77 (opened at src/daemon/threads/session-worker.ts:184) and, on the thread that hosts shared state, the start-up local understandingService in src/daemon/index.ts:446 (opened at src/daemon/index.ts:523; not module-scope, so outside the scanner), run registry src/daemon/workflow-run-registry.ts) are known to have one owner; all other module-scope state a session worker loads is unclassified. After: every such value is classified with a reason, and each value classified one-owner or shared-store is in fact owned or stored that way; values found to need a single copy that do not have one are moved (their methods routed to the owner, or the value put in an existing cross-thread store).

errorCases.scenario: A change adds a module-scope mutable declaration in a file the session worker loads, without classifying it.
errorCases.detection: The guard test compares moduleStateInventory's keys with the fixture's keys; the new key is missing from the fixture.
errorCases.response: The test fails naming the key and asking for a class and reason; nothing is excluded automatically.
errorCases.userImpact: The author classifies the new state (or makes it per-call) before the change can land.

errorCases.scenario: A classified declaration is renamed, moved to another file, or removed.
errorCases.detection: A fixture key no longer appears in moduleStateInventory's output.
errorCases.response: The test fails naming the stale key, so the fixture never keeps entries for state that no longer exists.
errorCases.userImpact: The author updates the key (keeping or revisiting the classification).

errorCases.scenario: A fixture entry has no class, an unknown class, a one-owner entry with no owner, or a reason under 40 characters.
errorCases.detection: The guard validates every entry's fields.
errorCases.response: The test fails naming the entry and the missing or invalid field.
errorCases.userImpact: None at runtime; the inventory stays reviewable.

errorCases.scenario: A one-owner entry names the shared-state worker but no method family routed there serves it.
errorCases.detection: For each one-owner entry with owner 'shared-state', the guard checks that the entry names a method prefix covered by SHARED_STATE_METHODS or IN_DAEMON_SHARED_METHODS.
errorCases.response: The test fails naming the entry; the value is either routed (a move) or reclassified with a correct reason.
errorCases.userImpact: A value claimed to have one owner cannot silently exist per worker.

errorCases.scenario: The scanner cannot build the program (unreadable tsconfig).
errorCases.response: The test fails with that error.

edgeCases.input: A const array or object literal that is only read (a lookup table)
edgeCases.expected: Not reported: the type checker finds no write to it.

edgeCases.input: A const literal mutated through an alias the checker cannot follow (passed to a function that pushes into it)
edgeCases.expected: May be missed by the write filter; the LLD accepts this limit, and the classification pass reviews the const literals in files that hold other state.

edgeCases.input: A `let` used only as a test seam (classifierImpl, depsForTest)
edgeCases.expected: Reported and classified per-thread: a test sets it in one thread for that thread.

edgeCases.input: A per-thread store handle (src/db/graph/store.ts _instance) over files shared by every thread
edgeCases.expected: Reported and classified per-thread with the reason that each thread opens its own handle over the shared LMDB/Lance files.

edgeCases.input: A declaration reached only through a dynamic import()
edgeCases.expected: Reported: the closure follows dynamic imports with a string-literal specifier.

edgeCases.input: A module only loaded on the admin or indexing worker or the main thread
edgeCases.expected: Not in the session worker's closure, so not reported.

edgeCases.input: One of the four s3 families (sessionPool in src/daemon/chat-handler.ts, the todos bus, the understanding service, the run registry board)
edgeCases.expected: Classified one-owner (shared-state) or shared-store as s3 made them, with the s3 mechanism as the reason.

migration.stateBefore: Per the s1 bundles: a session worker loads nearly all of src/ (548 files) and with it 583 top-level candidates for module-scope state; only the four s3 families are known to have one owner (src/daemon/threads/method-class.ts:262 routing, src/daemon/workflow-run-registry.ts:91 board), and no test notices new module-scope state. The only source inventory, src/daemon/db/__tests__/session-source-inventory.test.ts, covers provider/connection boundary sites, not module state.
migration.stateAfter: A test-side scanner lists every module-scope mutable declaration in the session worker's import closure; a reviewed fixture classifies each one (per-thread, shared-store or one-owner with its owner) with a reason; a guard test fails on any unclassified, stale or invalid entry and on a shared-state one-owner entry whose family is not routed. Values found to need one copy but lacking one are moved to an owner the s3 way.

migrationSteps.action: Add the test-side scanner beside the existing source inventory, with a unit test over a temporary project covering each declaration kind, read-only and frozen tables, dynamic imports and out-of-closure modules.
Generate the list of sites over the real source tree and classify every entry with a class, owner where needed, and a reason; record the classification as the fixture.
Add the guard test comparing the scanner's output with the fixture and validating each entry, including the shared-state routing check.

For each entry classified one-owner or shared-store that is not already owned or stored that way, move it: route its method family to the owner (as s3 did with SHARED_STATE_METHODS) or keep it in an existing cross-thread store, with a two-session-worker test. If a needed move is large enough to deserve its own design, stop and raise it as a separate tracked item instead of folding it in.
Refresh the session-source inventory entries for any production file a move edits.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API, IPC method or payload changes. The scanner, fixture and guard are test-side. A move that routes a method family to the shared-state worker changes only which thread serves it; replies are unchanged, as with s3's routing. Threads stay behind daemon.threads.enabled (default off).

alternativesConsidered.name: Declaration-level inventory fixture with a compiler scanner over the session worker's import closure
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A test-side scanner (a ts.Program like connectionSourceInventory) lists every module-scope mutable declaration the session worker can load; a JSON fixture keyed by file#name classifies each with a reason; the guard fails on any unclassified or stale key.
alternativesConsidered.approach: A new scanner beside connectionSourceInventory walks the static and dynamic import closure from src/daemon/threads/session-worker.ts and collects, per file, the top-level declarations that hold mutable state: every `let`/`var`, and every `const` whose initializer is a mutable container (new Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet/AsyncLocalStorage or another constructed instance, or an array/object literal) unless it is frozen (`as const`, Object.freeze) or the type checker finds no write to it (assignment, property write, or a mutating method call such as set/add/delete/push/splice) anywhere in the program. A fixture keyed by `<file>#<name>` gives each a class: `per-thread` (a separate copy per thread is correct: caches of immutable or re-readable data, test seams, per-thread handles over shared files, logger setup), `shared-store` (the value lives in a cross-thread store: the lock block, the status board, LMDB/Lance) or `one-owner` (only one thread may hold it; names the owner and how calls reach it, as s3's shared-state routing does), plus a reason of at least 40 characters. The guard test fails when a declaration is missing from the fixture, when a fixture key no longer exists, or when an entry has no valid class or reason; it does not digest source, so editing a classified file does not fail it. Any declaration classified one-owner or shared-store that is not already so is moved to its owner the s3 way (route its methods to the owning worker, or put the value in an existing cross-thread store).
pros: Per-declaration classification, which is exactly what the work item asks for, and reviewable in one place
Reuses the existing ts.Program approach and repo tsconfig; no new dependency
No source digests: classified files can be edited freely; only new or removed mutable state trips the guard
Write-reference filtering drops the read-only const tables, keeping the inventory to real state
cons: A few hundred entries to classify by hand once
Write detection through aliases (a value passed to a function that mutates it) can miss a write, so a filtered-out const may in fact be mutated

alternativesConsidered.name: File-level classification in the existing session-source inventory style
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Extend the session-source inventory pattern: one entry per file that holds module-scope mutable state, with a class and rationale for the file and a whole-file source digest.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Reuse the session-source-inventory shape: a fixture keyed by file listing the file's mutable declarations, one classification and rationale per file, and a sourceDigest so any edit forces re-inspection. The guard fails on a new or removed file, a changed declaration list, or a changed digest. Moves as in a1.
pros: Smallest fixture (about 280 files instead of several hundred declarations)
Same shape and refresh tool as the existing inventory
cons: One class per file is wrong where a file mixes per-thread caches with state that needs one owner (src/db/graph/store.ts holds both handles and health broadcast state)
The whole-file digest fails the test on every edit to any of ~280 files, the friction this session's builds already hit with the session-source inventory
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Classifies files, not values, and the source digest fails the guard on every edit to ~280 files.

alternativesConsidered.name: Classification comments at each declaration, checked by the guard
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each module-scope mutable declaration carries a `// thread-state: <class> — <reason>` comment; the guard scans the same closure and fails on any declaration without a valid comment.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The scanner of a1 finds the declarations; instead of a fixture, each declaration has a leading comment naming its class and reason, which the guard parses. New state fails until its author writes the comment next to it. Moves as in a1.
pros: The classification sits next to the code, visible to whoever edits it
No separate fixture to keep in sync
cons: Touches a few hundred source files with comment-only edits, across areas other sessions are editing (src/daemon/db), and each touched file then needs the session-source inventory refreshed
No single reviewable list of the classification
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Classifies values, but by editing a few hundred source files, many in areas another session is changing.
